subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a stable cross-language agent-runtime protocol for embedded/no-Node implementations, and if so which constrained runtime should define the first conformance target?
rationale: The remaining work is a broad public architecture and compatibility commitment; repository evidence establishes the gap but cannot decide whether OpenClaw should own and version that external protocol.

options.title: Sponsor a minimal protocol
options.body: Define a narrow versioned contract around the existing agent-core concepts and require one non-Node conformance implementation before expanding scope.

options.title: Keep TypeScript-only core
options.body: Treat `@openclaw/agent-core` as the supported portability boundary and document embedded projects as independent implementations rather than compatible OpenClaw runtimes.

options.title: Defer protocol ownership
options.body: Leave the discussion open without committing to an ABI until multiple external runtimes demonstrate concrete interoperability requirements.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a minimal protocol
recommendation.body: Define a narrow versioned contract around the existing agent-core concepts and require one non-Node conformance implementation before expanding scope.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current agent-core boundary and authored the prior direction review for this issue.
